title: 7 Readiness Indexes | Your Child’s Next Step | PinnacleAI®
directAnswer: PinnacleAI’s Seven Readiness Indexes are separate software views for School, Speech, Motor, Study IQ, Behavior, Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion. They help a professional interpret relevant abilities and support needs when planning and reviewing a child’s next everyday opportunity.
lifePurpose: Readiness becomes useful when your family understands what the child can do, the support that helps, the opportunity to work toward and how the team will review it. The child’s life gives the measurements their direction.

readinessAreas.name: School Readiness
readinessAreas.question: What helps my child take part in the school day?
readinessAreas.meaning: Consider the abilities and support needed to enter and sustain a learning environment.
readinessAreas.moment: Joining a short group activity, moving between familiar routines or asking an adult for help.
readinessAreas.discuss: Which classroom opportunity fits now? What communication, sensory, learning or environmental support would make it accessible?

readinessAreas.name: Speech Readiness
readinessAreas.question: How can my child be understood by another person?
readinessAreas.meaning: Consider functional communication in the next environment, including the communication methods the child uses.
readinessAreas.moment: Making a choice, asking for a turn or telling someone that help or a break is needed.
readinessAreas.discuss: Can the message be understood at home and in the next setting? Would speech, a gesture, a picture or another suitable aid help?

readinessAreas.name: Motor Readiness
readinessAreas.question: What helps my child move, reach and take part?
readinessAreas.meaning: Consider how gross and fine movement support participation and self-care.
readinessAreas.moment: Reaching a play surface, handling a toy, managing a spoon or taking part in dressing.
readinessAreas.discuss: What can the child already do? Would a different position, tool, environment or professionally guided activity make participation easier?

readinessAreas.name: Study IQ Readiness
readinessAreas.question: What helps my child understand and learn the next step?
readinessAreas.meaning: The dossier describes attention, sequencing and comprehension in relation to structured learning. “Study IQ” is the name printed in the BIS schedule.
readinessAreas.moment: Following a short picture sequence, understanding a familiar instruction or learning through a shared activity.
readinessAreas.discuss: What helps understanding: a demonstration, fewer steps, a visual cue, more time or a different activity? This view is not a stand-alone IQ test.

readinessAreas.name: Behavior Readiness
readinessAreas.question: What helps my child feel comfortable enough to participate?
readinessAreas.meaning: Consider regulation in group settings and the conditions or support that make participation possible.
readinessAreas.moment: Moving from one activity to another, communicating discomfort or choosing a manageable break.
readinessAreas.discuss: What is the child communicating? How can the setting, predictability, choices or appropriate support help?

readinessAreas.name: Self Sufficiency Index
readinessAreas.question: What can become more of my child’s own everyday life?
readinessAreas.meaning: Consider participation and independence in meaningful activities of daily living.
readinessAreas.moment: Choosing clothes, taking part in a meal, managing part of a routine or asking for useful help.
readinessAreas.discuss: Which part does the child do now, with what support? What next step matters to the child and family? Adaptations can remain part of independence.

readinessAreas.name: Mainstream Inclusion Index
readinessAreas.question: What helps my child learn, play and belong with others?
readinessAreas.meaning: Consider participation in an inclusive setting and the support that remains useful.
readinessAreas.moment: Joining peers in play, taking part in a classroom activity or participating in a family or community occasion.
readinessAreas.discuss: What opportunity is meaningful, what does the setting need to provide, and how will the child’s comfort and participation be reviewed? Inclusion is not a reward earned by a score.

illustrativeExample.title: “My child wants to join the game.”
illustrativeExample.intro: One goal can bring several views together. This illustrative planning example shows the conversation, not an actual child’s report or an observed outcome.
steps: Start with the life the family wants
The family wants their child to join a short building game with a familiar peer. The child enjoys blocks and chooses when to take part.
The child already points to a preferred block. A calm space and familiar adult help. The professional asks about communication, access to the activity and comfort in a group.
Speech and Mainstream Inclusion help frame communication and participation. School, Motor or Behavior may add useful context. Every view does not become an automatic therapy target.
Practise an accessible way to request a turn—such as a word, gesture or picture—with an appropriate professional. Agree how the adult and peer will respond and how the child can request a break.
Make it usable at home and school
Try a short, comfortable opportunity in familiar play. With the family’s consent, the teacher can use the same helpful cue. The child’s choice and enjoyment matter alongside taking a turn.
Bring the real experience back into review

Notice what happened, with whom, in which setting and with what help. The professional and family decide whether to continue, adapt the activity, change support or reassess. A rising number alone cannot make that decision.

A professional explains the current report and which readiness views matter.
Agree a meaningful goal, suitable people and methods, and manageable practice.

questions.question: What are the seven PinnacleAI Readiness Indexes?
questions.answer: The BIS schedule names School Readiness, Speech Readiness, Motor Readiness, Study IQ Readiness, Behavior Readiness, Self Sufficiency Index and Mainstream Inclusion Index. They are separate software views used with professional interpretation to support planning and review.

questions.question: How are readiness indexes different from AbilityScore®?
questions.answer: AbilityScore® contributes a composite starting picture of developmental abilities. Readiness views focus the discussion on a relevant opportunity, such as communication in a new setting or participation at school. The team interprets both with the child’s context and actual observations.

questions.question: Does every child need all seven indexes or all four therapies?
questions.answer: A professional decides what is appropriate to assess and discuss. The family’s priority, the child’s abilities, comfort and context determine the relevant views and support. The seven areas do not prescribe a fixed package of therapies.

questions.question: Does a School Readiness Index guarantee admission?
questions.answer: No. It helps a professional and family discuss relevant abilities and support. The school makes its admission decisions, and meaningful inclusion also depends on the environment and appropriate support.

questions.question: Is Study IQ Readiness an IQ test or a diagnosis?
questions.answer: No. Study IQ is the area name printed in the BIS schedule. The dossier relates it to attention, sequencing and comprehension for learning. PinnacleAI is licensed as non-diagnostic developmental-support software.

questions.question: How should I interpret a readiness number?
questions.answer: Ask which report version and display scale are being used, what information informed the view, what support or setting was recorded and what it means for the next goal. Compare like-for-like information with a professional; there is no universal pass mark published on this page.

questions.question: Can our family and teacher help with the review?
questions.answer: Yes. Share relevant observations about what the child does, the setting, comfort and support that helped. School observations can contribute with appropriate consent and access. The professional uses them to interpret and review the plan.

questions.question: How do we begin, and is the first call free?
questions.answer: Call 9100 181 181 to discuss your child’s current goal and ask about a suitable assessment and professional. Telephone guidance is free. The team explains the centre, visit arrangements and any assessment or therapy fees before you decide.
